title: Unbounded ordinary etale compact-support comparisons
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and work on the small etale sites with constant-ring module sheaves and unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. All schemes below are Noetherian, meaning they admit finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Each morphism to which $R(-)_!$ is applied is separated and of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and has a compactification [def-asd-compactifiable]. For $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,r:\overline X\to Y)$ put $Rf_!^c=Rr_*Dj_!$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support].

The proper-refinement comparisons, restricting to the identity on $X$, are canonical natural isomorphisms between these functors. Identity refinements give identities and composites give composites; comparison through a common refinement is independent of that refinement and satisfies the cocycle identity. Write $Rf_!$ for the resulting compactification-independent functor. For composable $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z$ there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$\alpha_{g,f}:Rg_!Rf_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R(gf)_!,$$
independent of compactification choices, compatible with refinement comparisons and identities, and associative for three morphisms. Its normalization is the proper/open tower comparison: choose $Y\xrightarrow{i}\overline Y\xrightarrow{s}Z$ and $X\xrightarrow{a}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}\overline Y$ compactifying $g$ and $if$, respectively, put $V=\overline X\times_{\overline Y}Y$, and write $b:V\hookrightarrow\overline X$, $q:V\to Y$, $j:X\hookrightarrow V$, so $bj=a$. Then $\alpha_{g,f}$ is $Rs_*$ of the proper/open interchange $Di_!Rq_*\to Rp_*Db_!$, followed by the direct-image and open-extension composition identifications [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition, lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition]. The interchange is adjoint under $Di_!\dashv i^*$ to the inverse of the proper open-restriction exchange $i^*Rp_*\cong Rq_*b^*$, with $b^*Db_!\cong1$ [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality].

For a cartesian square [def-pc-fibre-product] with $f:X\to Y$, $v:Y'\to Y$, $X'=X\times_Y Y'$, and projections $v':X'\to X$, $f':X'\to Y'$, the natural exchange
$$C_{f,v}:v^*Rf_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_!v'^*$$
is an isomorphism on every unbounded complex. On a chosen compactification it is the canonical proper exchange [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], followed by the inverse of the degreewise open-extension comparison [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map]. It is independent of compactification, compatible with identities, composite changes of base and the composition comparisons $\alpha$. The comparisons and exchanges restrict on bounded-below inputs to those of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons, thm-cbc-finite-torsion] with these same normalizations.

proof.text: Use the existing exact termwise inverse-image and open-extension functors and their derived adjunctions. Prove coherence of termwise inverse-image composition by descending the sheaf associativity and unit equations. Assemble these functors, their actual adjunctions and these equations into the private unbounded compact-support formalism. Identify its flexible proper compositor with the canonical total-right-derived compositor by comparing conjugates under the derived adjunctions; identify its open compositor by the adjunction unit criterion. These identifications preserve the actual maps, not merely their isomorphism classes.

proof.text: Identify the formalism square isomorphism and proper base-change map with the specified exact derived inverse-image square and its mate. Transport the left-derived exchange to exact termwise inverse image using the canonical left-derived/exact isomorphism; its unit and counit cancel by the mate equations. Identify the formalism open base change and proper/open exchange with the ordinary etale maps. Finite-coefficient proper base change gives the proper exchange axiom on unbounded inputs.

source.place: Tags 0F7H, 0F7L, and 0F7B(b): exact proper/open exchange normalizations.

proof.text: Identify the formalism refinement comparison with the existing proper-refinement comparison on a cartesian open square, and identify its common-refinement isomorphism with the existing compactification comparison. Apply the proved abstract compact-support-formalism identity and cocycle laws. Identify the formalism triangle compositor with the displayed proper/open tower compositor by its component formula and the canonical open and proper composition equations. Apply its every-triangle formula, associativity and identity laws and transport the results to the existing chosen compactifications. The concrete ofComp/ofRestrict triangle construction supplies the compatible tower directly; no separate existential compatible-tower theorem or staircase expansion is required.

source.place: Tags 0F7I--0F7K: common refinements, triangle independence, associativity and units.

proof.text: For the arbitrary-refinement normalization, first show uniqueness of the sheaf comparison specified by equality of its two maps into the proper direct image: that map is monic after the conservative open/closed restrictions, hence monic. On an injective complex, compute the right-derived unit using the K-injective fully faithful model and the exact derived-functor factorization. The derived normalization clause of the given family and this model identify its graph-normalized comparison with the sheaf-normalized construction on every K-injective representative. The localization universal property then identifies the natural transformations on the whole derived category. For a cartesian refinement, compare adjuncts under open extension and use the inverse proper exchange normalization. The family refinement clause gives the composition law for transports. For an arbitrary refinement, pass to its dense open restriction; both the dense refinement and its composite with the given refinement have cartesian open squares. The two cartesian identifications and cancellation of the invertible dense-refinement factor give the asserted comparison for the arbitrary refinement.

source.place: Tag 0F7B(b) graph normalization and Tag 0F7I refinement comparison; the natural-transformation equality is checked through K-injective representatives.

proof.text: The tower exchange is the mate of the inverse proper open-restriction exchange followed by the open-adjunction unit; this is the existing adjunct normalization. Express the compactification-relative shriek exchange as the pasted proper exchange and inverse open base change. The formalism refinement square proves independence of the compactification and identifies the chosen map with the transported existing unbounded exchange, hence proves its invertibility. Identity exchange follows from the horizontal pasting equation by cancelling the invertible exchange, rather than expanding the mate a second time.

source.place: Tag 0F7L: compactification independence, invertibility, and identity base change.

proof.text: For successive base changes, choose the composite compactification obtained by the two pullbacks and apply the formalism horizontal pasting equation. Transport its three compactification maps using the already established refinement independence; the pullback-refinement square is cartesian, so the comparison factors cancel. For compatibility with composition of morphisms, apply the proved formalism exchange/compositor pasting identity and replace each formalism map by its concrete exact-derived normalization. These are equalities of natural transformations and include the chosen inverse-image associator.

source.place: Tags 0F7J--0F7L: horizontal and vertical pasting of base-change maps.

proof.text: For bounded-below restriction, use the total-right-derived universal property to compare right-derived natural transformations, composition and the identity unit under the inclusion D+ into D. Exact functors commute with this inclusion on the nose; derive the corresponding unit, counit and square compatibilities for the actual derived adjunctions. This proves equality of proper exchange maps on bounded-below inputs. Apply it to the cartesian open-refinement exchanges, then to the two common-refinement factors and their inverses, to obtain the asserted compactification-comparison restriction.

source.place: Tags 0F7H--0F7L: the specified bounded-below restriction of the comparisons.

proof.text: Compare the bounded and unbounded open-extension compositors by their adjunction units; under D+ inclusion, both conjugates are the same exact inverse-image compositor. Use the derived-functor composition compatibility for the proper compositor and the preceding proper/open exchange compatibility. Express the inclusion comparison of a composite functor by whiskering its two inclusion comparisons. Generic natural-transformation pasting lemmas combine compatible horizontal and vertical composites, associators and functor isomorphisms. Apply their triangle formula to the proper/open tower, and identify its inclusion comparison with the candidate compact-support comparison. Transport this equation along the three compactification comparisons to the chosen functors, using the bounded and unbounded every-tower formulas and compositor pasting. The private interfaces state the maps using their concrete functors, so the specialization does not unfold the whole formalism.

source.place: Tags 0F7H--0F7K: equality of the normalized composition maps on bounded-below inputs.

proof.text: Finally paste the bounded/unbounded compatibility squares for proper exchange and inverse open base change, keeping the full inclusion comparison maps throughout the generic calculation. The concrete compactification exchange formula is exactly this pasted square. Normalize its associators and exact-functor identities, and obtain the asserted bounded-below exchange equality. No inference from equality of cohomology maps is used.

source.place: Tags 0F7H and 0F7L: equality of exchange maps on bounded-below inputs.

lean.statement: theorem unboundedEtaleCompactSupport_baseChange (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A] {X X' Y Y' : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian X'] [IsNoetherian Y] [IsNoetherian Y'] {f : X ⟶ Y} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {v : Y' ⟶ Y} {v' : X' ⟶ X} [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [HasCompactification f] [HasCompactification f'] [QuasiCompact f'] (sq : IsPullback v' f' f v) : IsIso (unboundedEtaleCompactSupportBaseChange A sq) ∧ ∀ c : Compactification f, unboundedEtaleCompactSupportBaseChange A sq = Functor.whiskerRight (rightDerivedLowerShriekIso A c).inv (upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) v).mapDerivedCategory ≫ unboundedEtaleCompactSupportExchange A sq c ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft (upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) v').mapDerivedCategory (rightDerivedLowerShriekIso A (c.ofIsPullback sq)).hom
lean.note: The module states the complete unbounded comparison package through the listed declarations: common-refinement identity/cocycle, arbitrary proper-refinement normalization, every-tower composition normalization, units and associativity, the proper-open adjunct normalization, exact proper/open exchange normalization, compactification independence, identity and composite base changes, compatibility with composition, and equality of the comparison/composition/exchange maps on bounded-below inputs. Helper definitions only assemble these canonical maps and transport the existing L-upper-star exchange to exact termwise inverse image. The refinement normalization holds for every existing graph-normalized family N; its nonemptiness is supplied by lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization, so it adds no assumption on the schemes or coefficients. No source statement was changed.
